---
title: "A formal home for computational pharmacy at Hanoi University of Pharmacy"
---

[University decision · 24 October 2025]{.eyebrow}

::: {.lede}
On 24 October 2025 the Rector of Hanoi University of Pharmacy, Nguyễn Hải
Nam, signed Decision 1114/QĐ-DHN establishing the **Unit of Computation and AI
Application Research** under the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Chemistry and
Technology. Four days later, Decision 1125/QĐ-DHN assigned Dr. Đỗ Thị Mai Dung the
duties of Head of the Unit.
:::

## Why a decision matters

Computational work had been going on in the Faculty for years before this, carried
by individual projects and individual students. What changed in October 2025 is
that it acquired a name, a mandate and a place on the University's organisational
chart. A unit can be given tasks, be held to them, and be built on. A collection
of side projects cannot.

## What the University asked the unit to do

The decision sets out the unit's function as advising the University and the
Faculty on organising and carrying out research that applies computation and
artificial intelligence, in both research and teaching. Its assigned tasks are
specific, and worth reading as a description of the work rather than as
administrative language:

::: {.skill-grid}
::: {.skill}
### Screening and design
Build computational and simulation models that identify compounds with potential
biological activity, aimed at the discovery and development of new drugs.
:::

::: {.skill}
### Pharmacokinetics and safety
Build models that predict pharmacokinetic parameters, toxicity and adverse
effects — the properties that decide whether an active compound can ever become a
medicine.
:::

::: {.skill}
### Simulation and mechanism
Apply quantum chemical calculation, molecular-level simulation and binding
affinity estimation to study how a structure acts on a molecular target, and why.
:::

::: {.skill}
### AI on large datasets
Apply artificial intelligence to network pharmacology and omics data, to find
therapeutic targets of natural compounds, medicinal materials and traditional
remedies.
:::

::: {.skill}
### Teaching and curriculum
Advise the Faculty and the University on developing training programmes that build
digital competence in the relevant fields.
:::

::: {.skill}
### People and collaboration
Connect research groups inside the Faculty and the University, provide
computational consultancy to groups working on drug development, and run research
training for school pupils and students in AI applied to medicine and pharmacy.
:::
:::

## What it does not say

The mandate is computational throughout. It does not mention chemical synthesis,
and that is accurate: the capacity to design a compound, make it and test it sits
in the **Faculty of Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology**, where it has existed
for far longer than the unit has. Roughly half of the group's published work
reports compounds that were actually made.

The unit's job is the other half of the loop, and the reason the two halves matter
together is that they share a corridor. A prediction can be checked by the people
who made the molecule, and what the assay says can change the model in the same
week. That is the thing being built here, and the October decisions are what made
it something the University recognises rather than something a few people did after
hours.
